brands.d: Eugene W. Castle's company, the leading US publisher of 8 mm and 16 mm home movies from 1937; part of Universal from 1947, Universal 8 from 1977, ended 1984.
Kent D. Eastin's Davenport, Iowa, film company selling complete 16 mm, 8 mm and Super 8 prints by mail order until the 1980s.
Dudley film distributor founded by Derek and Anne Simmonds, the world's largest Super 8 distributor in the 1970s and 1980s; closed 2011.

French film company that introduced the 9.5 mm gauge and Pathé Baby home cinema in 1922.
British arm selling 9.5 mm cameras, projectors and library films; bought out in 1959 and liquidated in 1960.

notes: All four old kinds kept; 9.5 mm print added. Home-distribution lines became archetypes: Derann and Ken Films (Super 8), Castle Films/Universal 8 (8 mm, 16 mm, Super 8), Blackhawk (16 mm), Pathé Baby and Pathéscope (9.5 mm). Sound/silent, colour/B&W, reel size and base as t. 35 mm print has no archetype (no home-distribution line attested). Film titles omitted throughout.
